head.label: Questions
head.title: Questions and answers
head.lead: If your question is not answered here, write to us by email.

items.a: Creators with a YouTube channel of 1,000 to 50,000 subscribers. A channel with fewer than 1,000 subscribers cannot join yet.
Fill out the application form. We ask for your name, your email, a link to your channel, what it is about and your subscriber count. A phone number is optional.
We reply within 2 working days. A person looks at your channel and chooses a sponsor that suits it, and we suggest that sponsor to you.

items.q: Which platforms do you work with?
items.a: YouTube, for now. Other platforms will come later.
Write to us by email. The address is on the contact page and at the bottom of every page.

items.q: Do I have to look for sponsors myself?
items.a: No. Finding the sponsor is our work. Your part is to apply, and to say yes or no to what we suggest.

items.q: How do you choose a sponsor for my channel?
items.a: By hand. A person looks at your channel and picks a sponsor that suits it. There is no automatic list and no algorithm.

items.q: Can I say no to a sponsor?
items.a: Yes. You can turn down any sponsor we suggest. The final say is yours.

items.q: Does the sponsor have a say?
items.a: Yes. A sponsor approves each channel we suggest to it. A deal goes ahead only when you and the sponsor both say yes.

items.q: I represent a brand. How do I start?
items.a: Send a short inquiry from the For brands page. Tell us what you want to promote and your budget range.
Joining is free. We take a commission from your fee once a deal is done. It is 10% on a sponsorship under $500, 8% from $500 to $1,999, and 5% at $2,000 or more.
Only once a deal is done. If there is no deal, there is no commission.

items.q: Do sponsors pay extra because of the commission?
items.a: No. The sponsor pays exactly the agreed fee and nothing extra. The commission comes out of your fee.
